summary:
# NOTES: Linda Carlton's Perilous Summer (Edith Lavell, A. L. Burt Co., 1932)

Single book. Front matter lists Linda Carlton Series: Air Pilot; Ocean Flight; Island Adventure; Perilous Summer. Dedicated "To My Husband Victor Lamasure Lavell."

## Characters
- **Linda Carlton**: 18, aviatrix, first US girl to fly NY-Paris alone. Flies autogiro "Ladybug." Blue eyes. Niece of Aunt Emily. Earlier: Atlantic flight, Okefenokee kidnapping/island adventure, Bellanca sold.
- **Aunt Emily (Miss Emily Carlton)**: raised Linda; fears airplanes, never flown; motherly; Green Falls bungalow; cook **Anna**.
- **Dot (Dorothy) Crowley**: Linda's chum, small, bubbly; boyfriend **Jim Valier** (drawls, eats sandwiches); mother Mrs. Crowley.
- **Amy / Helen Tower**: girl ~14, found on road in Wisconsin after hit-and-run; amnesia; fears ghosts and dark; Linda named her "Amy" after Amy Johnson. Real name Helen Tower. Granddaughter of Henry Adolph Tower. Nurse **Mrs. Smalley ("Nana")**, deaf, elderly.
- **Ralph Clavering**: Linda's devoted admirer, wealthy, Harvard (missing degree due to math condition); father **R. W. Clavering**; mother away at Bar Harbor visiting Aunt Kate. Gets autogiro. Jealous of Lord Dudley.
- **Kit (Kitty) Hulbert**: Ralph's married sister; husband **Lt. Tom Hulbert**, U.S. Flying Corps.
- **Harriman (Harry) Smith**: old friend, believed in Linda's Atlantic flight; recalled to work; passenger in hunt (replaced).
- **Lord Claude Dudley**: English, ~35, handsome, claims castle needing money; friend of John Kuhns; really **Ed Tower** (in disguise).
- **Mike (Michael) O'Malley**: Grand Rapids Star reporter, freckled farm boy, one of five brothers; brother **Pat** (phone company, truck with extension ladder).
- **Mrs. Elsie Fishberry ("Aunt Elsie")**: fake aunt; later claims to marry Ed Tower; abandons him.
- **Ed Tower (Edward Tower)**: Helen's uncle, brother of her father; gray car, gray wig/beard disguise; ran Helen down; set fire to house; posed as Lord Dudley.
- **Sue Emery, Sarah Wheeler, Madge & Bert Keen, Frank Lawlor, Joe Elliston** (Fleet plane, failed takeoff, wheel dug in sand bank): other flyers.
- **Leo Epstein**: lawyer; sent threatening telegram for $50,000 suit.
- **Mr. Irwin**: Linda's lawyer suggestion.
- **Mr. Hudson**: Vice-president, Chicago Trust Company.
- **John Kuhns**: Tom's friend.

## Chapter Events (in order)
**I. The Accident**: Linda and Dot fly "Ladybug" from Green Falls over Lake Michigan to Wisconsin, picnic lunch. Gray-bearded driver, car ~80 mph, hits girl walking by road. Linda and Dot land, first aid, girl amnesiac, fears ghosts/dark. Flew to Milwaukee at sunset; hospital. Wire to Aunt Emily. Dot: "caramel cake." Newspapers print pictures of Linda and Dot.

**II. The Lost Girl**: Next day girls visit. Girl named "Amy" (after Amy Johnson). Picnic on western lake shore. Ralph meets them at airport, announces own autogiro. Ralph–Linda banter. Amy frightened of dark. Lord Dudley phones? (no—later). Amy's table manners good.

**III. Planning the Treasure Hunt**: Party at Kit's; Tom announces airplane treasure hunt by Mr. Clavering; entries due Wednesday; start Saturday. Lt. Tom Hulbert. Linda worried about Amy; Aunt Emily reluctant. Morning: Ralph and Aunt Emily object. Linda takes Amy's photo for Grand Rapids.

**IV. A Stranger at Green Falls**: Linda and Harry go to Grand Rapids with Amy's pictures; Harry insists on lunch. Tennis matches at Club. Lord Dudley introduced by Tom; Linda mentions treasure hunt. Amy: "I've seen that man before." Linda thinks he looks like Ronald Colman.

**V. A Flying Engagement**: Mike O'Malley arrives at dawn; breakfast by cook. Lord Dudley phones, asks Linda to fly him to Chicago, lunch at Lakeside Inn. He proposes unspoken; kisses her hand. Linda wonders if in love. Ralph annoyed at canoe/beach.

**VI. The Telegram**: Telegram: "Am returning to-night with Tom for my answer. Love. Claude." Ralph gets autogiro in Ch. VII. Lord Dudley canoe proposal: elope; Linda refuses ("A year... six months"). Entries: Ralph, Dot, Linda + Harry (passenger). Seven planes: Tom & Kit Hulbert; Dot & Jim; Bert & Madge Keen; Frank Lawlor & Sue Emery; Joe Elliston & Sarah Wheeler; Ralph alone; Linda & Harry.

**VII. The Widow in Black**: Ralph's autogiro arrives; Linda flies it. Mike returns. Harry must leave; Linda takes Amy as passenger. Mrs. Fishberry arrives, claims "Helen," threatens suit; Mike asks for legal proof. Aunt Emily worried.

**VIII. Amy's Relatives**: Fishberry meets Ed Tower in Chicago apartment. Plot: Ed claims father's will hidden; Trust Company holds bonds; $100,000 estate; Ed says girl's father (his brother) died in car accident. Plan: get pictures, set house on fire Monday; marry Monday; sue Linda for $50,000. Fishberry to be insane-asylumed.

**IX. The Take-Off**: Saturday, Aunt Emily goes by boat to Lake Winnebago Inn. Start 10 am; Milwaukee then Columbus, Beaver Dam. Joe Elliston's wheel damaged. Storm at Columbus; Madge & Bert crash; Ralph drops out. Linda and Amy fly through storm. Clue: "Fly northwest, past Beaver Dam to Fox River... Lake Waupin... large old house of gray plaster, flat roof and tower... treasure in barn... bright red wrapping."

**X. The Treasure**: Storm again; spot Fox River, Lake Waupin. Red soap box and candy box, envelope "The Winner of the Treasure Hunt," check $1,000 signed R. W. Clavering. Linda gives Amy $500. Enter house; ghost in tower. Autogiro won't start (spark plug). Fishberry arrives; takes Amy to Chicago. Linda circles tower, sees skeletal ghost with glass eyes, moving hands.

**XI. The Return of the Flyers**: Joe and Sarah arrive by car. Ralph and Madge/Bert arrive by taxi. Ralph left plane at Columbus. Linda lands on Inn lawn 7:35. Dot and Linda plan to visit house Monday with Mike.

**XII. Trickery**: Fishberry tells Helen lies (Montana, Uncle Ed). Locks Helen in kitchen; leaves Saturday evening.

**XIII. The Haunted House**: Helen alone; finds Nana's photo in Bible; eats oatmeal; reads Bible; Sunday waits.

**XIV. Two Surprises for Linda**: Sunday telegram from Leo Epstein for $50,000. Aunt Emily: Daddy sailing for Paris. Lord Dudley returns with John Kuhns. Walks with Linda; suggests buying off Fishberry; suggests "Was there really a car?" Linda refuses. Sailing for England early next week.

**XV. The Ghost in the Tower**: Monday; Linda and Dot fly; Dot brings sandwiches. Linda lockpicks. Helen calls from kitchen window. Ghost removed (curtains, string-pulled hands, weights). Hidden closet: Henry Adolph Tower's will: house, grounds, $100,000 to Helen, $5,000 to Mrs. Smalley. Fire starts; Linda nearly dies; Mike O'Malley and Pat arrive with ladder.

**XVI. While the House Burned...**: Fishberry's perspective. Sunday phone call with Leo Epstein. Ed Tower in Milwaukee Central Hotel Monday. Plan to fetch Helen; Helen gone. Ed sets fire under staircase with oil-soaked cotton waste; left wig/beard in bushes; Fishberry drove off in his car; Ed walks five miles.

**XVII. The Rescue**: Mike drives Pat's truck; ladder rescue; Helen down first; Linda last, ladder catches fire; "Ladybug" saved. Picnic on road with Dot's sandwiches (10), peaches (6), two apple pies. Will recovered by Dot. Disguise found; Helen says uncle likely.

**XVIII. In Quest of the Money**: Night flight to Green Falls. Mrs. Smalley arrived; Helen reunited. Newspaper blames arson. Trust Company (Mr. Hudson) gave Ed bonds Sunday. Linda plans flight to Newport News, VA.

**XIX. A Clew to Follow**: Automat lunch. Fishberry reveals Ed took job with air-transport company at Newport News; leaving for England. Linda and Helen fly SE to Spring City, Ohio.

**XX. Flying Over the Mountains**: Thursday; storm; Allegheny Mountains; crash into mountainside; Linda repairs autogiro; night in woods; deer.

**XXI. A Strange Landing**: Friday, Newport News. Transport left 9 am (missed by sixty minutes). Lt. Melville Pride's precedent. Linda lands on ship's deck, dropped mail bag. Captain. "Lord Dudley" revealed to be Ed Tower by Helen. Search finds $50,000 bonds and $50,000 cash. Pilot flies Ed back. Linda and Helen fly home via Baltimore (banker friend of father), reach Green Falls Monday afternoon. Helen reunited with Mrs. Smalley.

## Advertisements at end
Burt series ads (Betty Lee, Jean Mary, Girl Scouts, Merry Lynn, Marjorie Dean, Ann Sterling). Not story content.
